sections: Suits and suit packages

Our usual new-garment offers focus on suits and suit packages. Standalone shirts, trousers and coats may be available by arrangement for existing customers, subject to assessment and quotation. A two-piece suit includes a jacket/coat and trousers. A three-piece suit includes a jacket/coat, trousers and waistcoat. A full-set package may add a shirt and necktie; neither is automatically included in the standard suit price. Skirt-suit requests require a separate quotation and confirmation.
Designed around your preferences
Explore the design, proportions, colours and available fabric options with the team. Final details, materials and feasibility are agreed before an order.
Bring your ideas or your fabric

Bring sketches, reference photographs or cloth you already own. Discuss the design direction and ask the team to assess fabric quantity, suitability and any additional materials before agreeing the garment.
Measurements, fittings and finish
Arrange personal measurements, discuss fit and attend the agreed fitting appointments. Production timing and collection or delivery arrangements are confirmed for your order.

sections: Plan the complete order

Usual custom-tailoring planning windows are 7–10 working days for standard orders and 3–4 working days for express orders, subject to availability. These windows allow for purchasing, tailoring, agreed fittings, cleaning, packaging and delivery. Special designs have an individually agreed timeline. Confirm the actual completion date after the order is assessed and fittings are scheduled.
Express charges

Express custom tailoring adds 35% of the original standard suit price: express total = standard suit price × 1.35. This applies across all four suit collections. Separately priced shirts, accessories, transport, mobile visits and other extras are outside that calculation base. Special or nonstandard work receives an individually agreed quotation.
Confirm before you proceed
The team confirms feasibility, the full quotation, fitting appointments and the actual completion date before accepting an urgent order. An enquiry does not reserve production capacity.
